title: Optimize hash table usage in dissectors
description:
This MR mainly focuses on hash tables used to store UATs. The main changes are:
- Avoid allocating the keys on insertion when they are 32-bit IDs, and avoid strdup when they are strings (for 64-bit IDs we still allocate the key, since `GUINT_TO_POINTER` only works with ints up to 32-bit)
- Avoid allocating or duplicating keys for lookups
- Remove now mostly empty functions
- Don't delete empty hash tables. This way we make sure they are always non-null
- Fix an issue with `data_xcp_memory_addresses` being defined with `g_int_equal` but using 64-bit keys

Are you sure that removing this workaround is ok? It was necessary to make sure that Wireshark did not work with inconsistent configs and crash...

UPDATE: the reset CBs should be enough. Let us hope that not a crash is introduced by removing this.

I cannot remember how to reproduce the bug from back then.

However, this change introduces asserts failing:

`g_hash_table_lookup: assertion 'hash_table != NULL' failed`

I removed this code because it meant handling more cases without apparent reason (except saving a little bit of memory on empty tables).

As for the NULL check, I thought it was not necessary, since other dissectors get away without it. Probably they are broken too.

Doesn't the post-update callback get called every time, making sure the hash table is initialized?

Unfortunately, post-update is not called every time. If the UAT cannot be loaded (because format changed, bug in file, etc.) the post-update is not called. That was the main reason that we had sporadic issues in the past. So you cannot assume that the post-update is called.

In the past, I was not sure that even the reset was called, so we went that way. After testing, it seems that reset is called everytime, so that's why I added them.
Also see  https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/17227

I check a bit. FIrst test show that strings from UAT can get broken as Wireshark reads already freed data.

This MR has created unsafe memory access in some of the protocols affected, which may or may not crash Wireshark.
mentioned in issue #20360
This is needed! Removing the NULL check leads to asserts failing here.
If you do not use g_strdup, you need to guarantee that hashtable is always in sync with the data. Since this is not the case, this leads to unsafe memory access.
Isn't it kept aligned by the post-update callback? Is there the possibility that memory is accessed after the string is freed, but before the callback is called?

See above.

UAT is removed but post-update might not be called, if UAT file has an issue. Now the HT references memory that is freed. :disappointed:
Same here. NULL check is still needed.

Here a NULL check is missing.

It would be better to keep the ht_lookup_channel_config to have the NULL check there and not spread it around.

Same here.

ht_lookup_channel_config should be kept, so that the NULL check can live there.
See above... ht_lookup_name should stay, so that check for NULL is back.
For the first file, I tried to fix the issues: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18850

@LarsVoelker I see that you already prepared some MRs. First of all, sorry for making you do unnecessary work. Second, let me know if something is still missing.

I tried to test all protocols as good as possible and think the MRs are ready.

I will mark them as ready. Please also test, when they are in because it was quite some work and I want to make sure that I did not miss anything as testing so many UATs is quite a lot of work.

Ok, I marked all as ready.

Overall, trying to avoid the strdup/malloc/etc. was a good idea. The problem is that the UAT behavior is a bit complicated, especially in error cases. So the code evolved over a long time to cover different errors encountered before.

We should both check again, after everything is merged but I am pretty confident that consequently using resets and checking the HTs for NULL should be fine and reduce the warnings too.
